name: Deep-Fried Bean Curd With Oyster Sauce
author: Robert Farrar Capon

ingredients.raw: 1 pound firm tofu (bean curd), cut into 1-inch cubes
4 large ribs bok choy, cut into ¼-inch slices
2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons cold water
ingredients.item: cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons cold water

ingredients.raw: 2 scallions, trimmed and cut into ¼-inch pieces
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and cut into ¼-inch pieces

steps.text: In a wok, heat the oil for deep frying to 375 degrees, or until a piece of scallion placed in the oil bubbles and sizzles rapidly. Pat the tofu cubes dry with a paper towel. Fry the cubes in the oil for about 5 minutes, or until they are golden brown. Drain on paper towels and set aside. When the cubes are cool, cut each one in half.

Pour off the frying oil from the wok. Over high heat, add the peanut oil to the wok, then the garlic and brown bean sauce, and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the fried bean curd pieces, the water and the bok choy and bring to a boil. Cover the wok, lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Uncover, raise the heat, add the sake or sherry, the sugar and as much of the cornstarch mixture as is needed to thicken the dish, stirring constantly. Add the oyster sauce and scallions and mix well. Garnish with coriander and serve with plain boiled rice.

ingredients.raw: medium-size eggplants, about ¾ pound each
½ teaspoon finely chopped fresh rosemary, or half that amount dried
6 cups corn, peanut or vegetable oil

steps.text: Peel eggplants and cut each crosswise into ¾-inch-thick slices. Cut slices into sticks, each about ¾ inch wide. There should be about 6 cups.
Put egg in a large mixing bowl and add water, rosemary, salt, pepper and Parmesan cheese. Beat well.
Dip eggplant pieces in flour to coat well. Put pieces in egg mixture. Use fingers to coat pieces well.
Put bread crumbs in a flat dish and put egg-coated eggplant pieces in. Toss to coat uniformly. Transfer eggplant to a flat dish.

Heat oil in a deep fryer or kettle to 375 degrees. Add half the eggplant pieces and cook 3 minutes, or until crisp and golden brown. Drain thoroughly. Repeat, deep-frying with remaining eggplant. Serve hot.

name: Deviled Crab Meat and Chicory Salad With Egg Dressing
author: David Tanis

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon fruity extra virgin olive oil
8 ounces mixed salad greens like treviso, radicchio, Belgian endive and curly endive (frisée), cut in 1-inch ribbons
ingredients.preparation: radicchio, Belgian endive and curly endive (frisée), cut in 1-inch ribbons

ingredients.raw: ½ cup thinly sliced celery and leaves, from inner tender stalks
1 pound fresh jumbo lump crab meat
1 small Meyer lemon, cut in very thin slices, then half-moons, optional
ingredients.preparation: cut in very thin slices, then half-moons

steps.text: Make the dressing: Heat the cream to just under a boil, using a small pan over medium heat. Take off the heat. In a small stainless steel, Pyrex or ceramic mixing bowl, beat together the egg yolks, vinegar and lemon juice with a wire whisk. Whisk in the Dijon mustard, dry mustard, salt, cayenne and black pepper.

Place the mixing bowl in a pan of simmering water (or use a double boiler). Whisking constantly, add the hot cream in a slow stream. Continue to whisk, taking care not to let the mixture curdle, until the sauce looks like a thick milkshake, about 2 to 3 minutes.

Remove the sauce from the heat and whisk in the olive oil. Transfer to a chilled container and refrigerate. The dressing will thicken a bit more when cold. Can be made a day in advance. Makes about 1 cup.

To make the salad, put the chicories or salad greens and celery in a large salad bowl. Sprinkle with a little salt and dress with about 2 tablespoons of the dressing. Mix the remaining dressing with the crab meat, folding gently to incorporate. To serve, put dressed salad greens on individual plates and top with a large spoonful of crab meat. Garnish with chives and thin slices of Meyer lemon if desired.

name: Deviled Eggs With Chile and Lime
author: David Tanis
description: Everyone loves deviled eggs, right? They’re a little bit fiddly but worth the effort, and these have a nice kick and plenty of flavor. Take care halving the eggs to remove the cooked yolks so you don’t damage the cooked egg white. Then, mash the yolks in a small bowl with the seasonings: Dijon mustard, serrano chile, lime zest and juice and chopped dill, mint or tarragon. Here, softened butter replaces the traditional mayo for a creamy texture without worry. Though the stuffed eggs look fine simply sprinkled with snipped chives, they are spectacular with a few bright marigold petals on top (or other edible flowers like calendula or nasturtium).

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons softened unsalted butter or mayonnaise
1 teaspoon lime zest plus 2 tablespoons lime juice (from 1 lime)
ingredients.item: lime zest plus 2 tablespoons lime juice (from 1 lime)

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon very finely chopped serrano chile (remove seeds for milder heat)
ingredients.item: very finely chopped serrano chile (remove seeds for milder heat)

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon roughly chopped fresh mint, dill or tarragon
Yellow or orange edible flower petals, like marigold, calendula or nasturtium (optional), for garnish
ingredients.item: yellow or orange edible flower petals
ingredients.preparation: like marigold, calendula or nasturtium (optional), for garnish

steps.text: Set a medium pot of water over high heat and bring to a boil. Lower eggs into the pot and return to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Fill a bowl with cold tap water and ice.
Transfer eggs to the ice bath. When eggs are cool, forcefully tap each one all over to crack the shell. Return eggs to ice bath, so water seeps in. Peel eggs and blot on a towel.
Cut eggs in half lengthwise. With a small spoon, carefully remove yolks and place in a large bowl. Set the egg whites cut side up on a paper towel-lined plate.
To the yolks, add butter, lime zest and juice, mustard, chile and cayenne. Add salt and pepper to taste. Mash to a soft paste with a fork, then use a wooden spoon to thoroughly work the seasoning.

Stir in mint and most of the chives, reserving 2 pinches of chives for garnish. Taste and adjust seasoning. Spoon egg yolk mixture into the cups of the reserved egg whites, dividing it evenly among them.
Arrange egg halves on a platter. Sprinkle with flaky salt, remaining chives and petals, if using, and refrigerate until ready to serve. To serve, remove from the fridge and bring to room temperature.
